The title has a grammatical issue: "Added test configure valid static IPv6" should be "Add test to configure valid static IPv6" or "Added test to configure valid static IPv6". The body also lacks detail about what makes this test different from existing IPv6 tests.


In the body, explain that this test specifically validates IPv6 address normalization (leading zeros, zero compression) when configured from an IPv6 session.
Done
Ensure consistent spacing/alignment
Done

In the original Test Teardown Execution, Redfish.Logout is called before RedfishIPv6.Logout. 

After the change, Redfish.Logout is moved to Suite Teardown Execution. However, the new test case uses RedfishIPv6 session, and the test teardown only calls RedfishIPv6.Logout. This means if a test uses the regular Redfish session, it won't be logged out in the test teardown.


Recommendation: Verify that all existing tests properly handle their session cleanup. Consider keeping both logout calls in test teardown with Run Keyword And Ignore Error to ensure both session types are cleaned up.
Made this change as in previous code Redfish.Login was done in Suite Setup Execution. But Redfish.Logout was present in Test Teardown Execution and no Redfish.Login done for each tests.
Acknowledged

Variable names like ${ipv6_eliminate_zero} and ${ipv6_eliminate_zero1} are similar and could be confused.

Suggestion: Consider more descriptive names:

${ipv6_with_leading_zeros}        2001:0022:0033::0111
${ipv6_normalized_no_leading}     2001:22:33::111
${ipv6_with_first_hextet_zeros}   2001:0022:1133::1111
${ipv6_normalized_first_hextet}   2001:22:1133::1111
${ipv6_with_contiguous_zeros}     2001:0022:0000:0000:1:2:3:8
${ipv6_zero_compressed}           2001:22::1:2:3:8

Why: More descriptive names make the test intent clearer and reduce confusion.
Reusing the existing variables, changing the variable name might affect existing test cases. Will keep in mind to use more descriptive names for new variables created.
Done
